chunks: And from him, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdūs Al-Khalanjī, from his father Raḥīm, who said:

I said to Al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Ziyārah of the grave of Abū Al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) in Baghdad is upon us with difficulty, and we only visit him and send him Salām from behind the wall. What is the reward for the one who visits him?' He said, and he said to him, 'By Allāh, it is the same as the reward for the one who visits the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Kazim from behind the wall in Baghdad?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Riḍm Al-Riḍā (a.s.) establishes a high standard of reward equivalence by comparing the visitor of Imam Al-Kāẓim (a.s.) in Baghdad to the visitor of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.), emphasizing that physical proximity is secondary to sincere devotion. This hadith, recorded by Ibn Qulawayh, highlights the accessibility of spiritual merit even when geographical or structural barriers prevent direct contact with the shrine. It underscores the Shia principle that the reward for Ziyārah is not diminished by hardship or distance, provided the intent and effort are genuine.
